title: Aurora shift synopsis & escalation ledger
content:
Shift summary (Aurora window, 03-Jul-2026):

- Primary objective: maintain <120ms p50 for hosted-api generation routes, validate new cache TTL tweak on kv-prefix cache, and triage two escalations from telemetry.
- Handover notes: incoming shift picked up at 07:00 UTC; wind-down at 15:00 UTC. Briefed by on-call; all runbook toggles accessible via /ops/runbook CLI.

Incidents observed (timeline + quick outcomes):

1) Incident INC-1973 — transient request spikes to /v1/generate (08:12–08:29 UTC)
   - Symptom: abrupt p95 token latency increase from 540ms -> ~1.8s on one replica pool. Error rate stayed low, no 5xx spike.
   - Immediate action: scaled dedicated pool by +2 replicas (manual) at 08:15; throttled low-priority tenant routing for 6m to relieve pressure.
   - Root cause (hypothesis): uneven KV cache hot-keys causing CPU stalls during KV cache reloads on affected hosts.
   - Short-term mitigation: pinned model variant to quantized fallback on affected hosts, flushed local prefix cache, and disabled the recent kv-ttl bump for that pool.
   - Follow-ups: instrumented additional perf counters (KV cache miss latency) and added a Canary alert for TTL-change regressions. See linked ticket INC-1973 for logs and flamegraphs.

2) Incident INC-1976 — embeddings ingestion backlog (12:41–13:10 UTC)
   - Symptom: embeddings-ingest queue length grew 6x after batch job started; consumer lag caused delayed downstream reranks.
   - Immediate action: applied consumer parallelism bump (workers +3) and increased EBS IOPS for the embeddings node group. Requeued highest-priority batches.
   - Root cause: batch job introduced an unexpected I/O pattern; autoscaling did not respond quickly due to conservative cpu-utilization threshold.
   - Follow-ups: update autoscaler config to include SQS queue depth threshold and add a preflight check for batch job i/o footprint. See INC-1976.

Configuration changes made during shift:
- Reverted kv-prefix-cache TTL change on pool-aurora-1. (reason: regression in local hot-key behavior)
- Manually scaled dedicated pool-aurora-1 by +2 replicas from 3 -> 5 for immediate stabilization.
- Temporary route restriction rule: route low-priority tenants to dedicated-burst lane for 10min window.
- Bumped embeddings-consumer parallelism from 4 -> 7 on node-group embeddings-03.

Runbook edits proposed (draft):
- Add a section "KV cache TTL rollback checklist" with exact CLI commands, required observability checks, and post-rollback smoke tests.
- Add an autoscaler tuning appendix: include queue-depth metric mapping to desired replica counts and recommended cooldowns for batch-heavy workloads.
- Clarify ownership: make infra-autoscaler team the default pager for SQS/queue-depth alerts; SRE oncall remains escalation path.

Telemetry and dashboards to inspect during follow-ups:
- prefix_cache.miss_latency (new counter instrumented during shift)
- hosted-api.p95_per_route with breakdown by replica and model-variant
- s3-ebs-iops and embeddings-node-read-latency (to validate I/O improvement)
- queue_depth.sqs_embeddings and autoscaler.scale_events (for regression test)

Open action items (assigned):
- Priya Raman: write the KV TTL rollback runbook appendix and add smoke-test steps. (ETA 2026-07-06)
- Ethan Walker: add canary alarm for kv-ttl-change and update alert runbook. (ETA 2026-07-05)
- Sofia Almeida: schedule a post-mortem sync with infra-autoscaler and embeddings owners to validate autoscaler thresholds. (ETA 2026-07-07)
- Liam Chen: backfill trace annotations for INC-1973 and attach CPU flamegraphs to the incident. (ETA 2026-07-04)

Notes to self / quick fragments: 
- Observed weird GC pauses on two hosts; correlate with docker image patch applied on 02-Jul. Might be unrelated but add to checklist.
- Consider adding a lightweight prefix-cache heatmap to the console to spot hot-key imbalances quickly.
- We were lucky: no user-facing 5xx and no SLA breaches. Need to preserve the manual scaling pattern as a temporary play but automate soon.

Handover to next shift (bullet checklist):
- Verify replicas for pool-aurora-1 remain stable at 5 and autoscaler adjustments are prevented until next maintenance window.
- Watch prefix_cache.miss_latency for any reintroduction after 2026-07-05 when TTL experiment resumes in a canary-only pool.
- Confirm embeddings consumer parallelism and EBS IOPS are still holding; revert if downstream latency increases.
- Keep INC-1973 and INC-1976 marked as "ongoing" until follow-ups completed and traces attached.

Escalation log (who was paged and when):
- 08:18 UTC: Infra lead (Ethan) paged via PagerDuty (ack 08:20) for unexpected latency trend.
- 12:45 UTC: Data-platform lead (Sofia) informed via Slack for embeddings backlog; coordinated IOPS increase.
- 13:05 UTC: CTO on standby (informational) for potential cross-customer impact; not escalated to exec call.

Post-shift retrospective notes (quick):
- Good: quick manual scaling stabilized p95 rapidly; team coordination between SRE + infra effective.
- Improve: need automated guardrails for KV cache experiments (canary percentage + auto-rollback triggers).
- Improve: autoscaler should consider queue depth for big batch jobs — existing CPU-based thresholds are slow.

References and raw attachments (where to find logs):
- INC-1973 logs + flamegraphs: https://logging.redwood.com/ops/INC-1973
- INC-1976 Kinesis/SQS traces: https://logging.redwood.com/ops/INC-1976
- PR with infra changes applied 02-Jul: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/452
- Slack thread summary: slack://thread/SRE-ops-aurora-2026-07-03

End of shift note — handover complete. Next shift: Amaya Patel (primary) / On-call SRE rotation. Please ping me if anything re-opens or if any rollback is required.

-- Priya
